title: Breaking: The Fog Rolled In
description: A wall of fog swallows the whole town in four minutes flat. Ronnie anchors it like a hurricane special, the station's brand new meteorologist watches her instruments give up, and callers report the fog is following them, taking their stuff, and possibly nesting.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: We're cutting away from the regular hour on Snazzie FM. This is breaking weather. A wall of fog has entered the town from the west, and folks, it is moving with intent.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It's fog, Ronnie. I can SEE it. I don't need a graphic.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're seeing the leading edge, Barry. That's exactly what it wants. We're calling this a situation. <p:0.3> Let's bring in our brand new meteorologist. Rhonda, you're on the air.

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: Thanks, Ronnie. So, good news, I have the radar up, and this is a classic low ceiling advection event. Totally normal. Nothing to worry about.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Normal. <p:0.3> And how fast did this normal event cover the town, Rhonda?

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: Four minutes.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Four minutes. <p:0.3> Folks, I'm upgrading us. This is now a developing situation. Todd's at the window. Todd, what are we looking at?

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: Yeah, hi, Ronnie. So I'm at the glass, and, um. <p:0.3> I can't see the parking lot. I can't see my car. I can't see the OTHER window, and that window is right there.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That's just fog being fog, Todd. It does that.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Hello, dear, yes, it took my wind chimes. <p:0.3> The fog came up the porch, and now my wind chimes are gone, and it's standing in my yard, and it's WATCHING.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Mildred, fog cannot watch you. <p:0.3> Rhonda, can fog watch her?

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: No. <p:0.3> No, that's, fog doesn't have a, hang on. The radar's doing something weird. There's a return where the yard is. A solid return. <p:0.3> Fog isn't solid.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: I'm driving THROUGH this thing, okay, and I want to report that I can no longer see the hood of my own car. <p:0.3> I am pulling over. <p:0.3> I am pulling over INTO more fog.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Then turn your hazards on and wait it out, that's the whole answer.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Barry, the hazards are ON, and the fog is the same color as the hazards now. <p:0.3> It learned the orange.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: It learned the orange. <p:0.3> Folks, that's an upgrade. We are now in a Level Four Atmospheric Event. Bring in the pets. Count your wind chimes.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Why would anyone count their wind chimes, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Because Mildred didn't, Barry. And now Mildred has none.

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: Okay, I need everyone calm, because the radar is. <p:0.3> The radar is reporting the system has stopped moving. It's just sitting over the town. <p:0.4> Systems don't sit. They pass through. This one parked.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: It's at the window now, dear. <p:0.3> Not the yard. The window. It brought the chimes back and hung them somewhere I can't reach.

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: Ronnie? <p:0.3> Update. There's a shape in it. Out by the lot. It's low, and it's moving, and I think. <p:0.4> I think the fog is building something.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Building something. Rhonda, confirm. <p:0.3> Is the weather building something?

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: I, the instruments, okay, the barometer flatlined and the radar. <p:0.3> The radar drew a face. <p:0.4> I'm not, I didn't tell it to do that. It's a smiley face right over the post office.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: A face. The radar drew a face.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: It moved my CAR, Barry! I pulled over, I closed my eyes for one second, and now I'm facing the other way! <p:0.3> The fog turned me around like a polite valet!

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: It's nesting, dear! <p:0.3> It's pulled my patio cushions into a little pile and it's sitting on them!

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Nesting. <p:0.3> Folks, weather does not nest. I'm upgrading us one more time. As of this moment, this is, frankly, a tenant.

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: The radar drew a doormat, Ronnie. <p:0.3> It drew a little welcome doormat. The instruments aren't reading the weather anymore. The instruments have just, accepted it.

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: Okay so. <p:0.3> Something's coming out of the fog. By the doors. It's small, it's, it's waddling, and it has, um. <p:0.4> It has a lawn chair.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: A lawn chair. <p:0.3> Whose lawn chair, Todd?

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: Okay so the goose has the lawn chair now. <p:0.3> A goose just walked out of the fog with a lawn chair. It's holding wind chimes in the other, the, the wing.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Those are MY chimes!

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: The goose isn't on the radar!

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Is the fog driving the goose?!

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It's a goose with a chair!

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: It set the chair DOWN!

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: It set the chair down. <p:0.4> Folks. <p:0.3> We are no longer classifying this as weather. <p:0.3> We are classifying it as a neighbor.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: I told you I could see it.

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: It drew a second face. <p:0.3> The radar. There are two faces now, Ronnie. They're next to each other. <p:0.4> Like they live here.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Then we welcome them. <p:0.3> The fog is not leaving, folks. By all readings, it has moved in. We'll be right back, soon as the goose vacates the lobby.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Tell it I'd like my chimes back, dear.
